# R426 — Current 4K prefill matrix-path capability and evidence limits

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only audit of one closed GEN record's named `engine-phase-lifetime` trace and the specified phase4k source. No command execution against the model, GPU, CLI, build, test, lint, AST, profiler, process/service, cleanup, or source edit. The only file written is this report. One mistake during this read-only audit: after the scoped trace review, I ran a narrow `rg` against the GEN record for two environment-variable names. It printed two matching recipe entries outside `engine-phase-lifetime`; I did not use those entries to infer runtime path selection. The protected prefill-GEMM contract record was not opened.

## Finding

The trace proves that this B570 runtime reported XeStrata's own prompt matrix kernels as **XMX** at startup. It does not prove which MoE product branch ran during the recorded 4K chunks. The trace has no `strata prefill route census`, `strata prefill timing`, per-call `gemm_path`, or service-event backend rows. Consequently the current source can establish which paths are eligible, and the log can establish the general XMX capability, but this run cannot establish MoE path counts, the actual per-expert M histogram, or an XMX-versus-MMQ/fallback timing split.

The model dimensions make the fallback XMX shapes legal: route uses top-16 for 512 experts; a 4,096-token chunk therefore has 65,536 routed rows and a uniform-distribution mean of 128 rows/expert (a calculation, not the measured histogram). Native expert products are GU `[M, 2560] × [2560, 1280]` and Down `[M, 640] × [640, 2560]`. They meet `xmx_gemm_ok`'s N/K divisibility limits; actual grouped support also needs 64-byte aligned operands and an available XMX device path. Current trace's startup report supports the latter at device level. It does not certify every call's pointers or selected dispatcher.

## What the trace establishes

The only inspected record is `/home/yayoi/.local/state/strata-sycl/post-reboot-tuning-20261007/main-layer-major-phase4k-prefix32k-first-row-root-v1/record.json`, SHA-256 `2b127c9731c93c93c6d7bc784780277b08c642d967bef57cff977d4357f15bca`. Within its named `engine-phase-lifetime` stdout/stderr, startup says the GPU is an Intel Arc B570 (160 compute units, 9.9 GiB) and reports “prompt matrix products on XeStrata's own kernels (XMX)”. The trace shows a 32,768-token prefill in 4,096-token chunks, checked layer-major uploads for 512 slots per layer, and a completed request. Its per-layer transfer and prompt summaries establish progress and correctness/close status, not product backend or service time.

In the inspected trace there are no lines beginning `strata prefill route census v1:`, `strata prefill timing:`, or `strata prefill service events:`; nor is there a per-call `gemm_path` / backend line. The current source can emit a transfer census when `STRATA_PREFILL_TRANSFER_COUNTS` is set, phase intervals with `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING`, and optional operation events through `STRATA_PREFILL_SERVICE_EVENTS`. Their absence means the current output cannot prove actual M distributions or use of XMX, MMQ, oneMath, DP4a, or the fused native expert GEMM for these MoE rows.

## Caller and capability conditions

`mmq::built()` calls `iq_mmq_usable()` on the active device and queue; the usability check requires reported matrix shape support and a successful accumulator-layout check (or AMD WMMA support). `iq_mmq::supported()` includes GGUF IQ3_S type 21. The current model's native GGUF expert dimensions fit that path. `mmq_plan()` enables it by default for native supported layers unless `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ` is explicitly off. Once enabled, `run_impl` takes the int8 MMQ branch and does not run the FP16 grouped-XMX/fused route for that layer. `STRATA_PREFILL_NATIVE_DEQUANT_BATCH=1` is additionally gated by `!use_mmq`; compact MoE scratch is also disabled while MMQ has a supported layer. Thus a logged/requested batch flag is not proof that batch dequant ran, and the user's no-MMQ setting (if any) is material. The named trace does not expose that decision.

When MMQ is off, the source has two relevant native paths. Resident experts with supported IQ format/dimensions, XMX availability, and `M <= kIqGemmTileRows` (256) can use `iq_gemm_grouped_f16`, which dequantizes tiles on the fly and multiplies with joint-matrix XMX. Experts outside that predicate use native dequant followed by grouped FP16 products. On this layer-major run the trace shows a 512-slot per-layer cache, so residency is available; it does not report each routed expert's M and therefore cannot say how many cross the 256-row predicate. Native batch dequant applies only to the non-MMQ branch.

The fallback `xmx_gemm_grouped` path dispatches a fixed 128×256 output tile, 16-lane subgroups, 32 subgroups per work-group, and 256-GRF kernels with K advanced by 32. It launches `G × ceil(max_rows/128) × ceil(N/256) × 32` work-groups; experts below a tile's row count cause early-returned row tiles. Here GU has 5 N tiles and Down has 10. The `M` histogram therefore changes idle row-tile work, the number of groups/launches, and useful XMX occupancy even though N/K pass the shape checks. The fused `iq_gemm_grouped_f16` uses 256×128 work-group tiles and up to 32 experts per call; its source comment explains it avoids dequantizing weights again for each row tile. No profiler/runtime occupancy, GRF spill count, or actual tile utilization is present in the current trace. Capability and launch geometry are source facts, not a measured occupancy result.

The host `Gemm::path()` report is a coarse path summary for the general prompt matrix products. In this build recipe oneMath is off; for individual grouped FP16 products `Gemm::f16_groups` uses oneMath only when the global path is DP4a, otherwise it lets the caller use its own XMX/joint-matrix or DP4a dispatch. That line cannot identify the MoE branch because MMQ bypasses this wrapper and the fused native IQ kernel has its own caller.

## Smallest useful next diagnostic

Use one bounded 4K-chunk timing diagnostic on the existing GEN route, with `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1` and `STRATA_PREFILL_TRANSFER_COUNTS=1`; retain the exact settings, runtime output, selected source hashes, request/result IDs, and correctness/close evidence. These existing outputs give per-phase GPU intervals and per-layer `mmq_enabled`, `mmq_direct` / `group_gather`, native dequant and active-route counts. They still need a small fixed-size row-count histogram added to the route census because today's census reports only totals and active-expert counts. Use bins aligned to both kernel row tiles (0, 1–15, 16–31, 32–63, 64–127, 128–255, 256+), plus max M and total routed rows; one record per layer, no per-expert output. Add bounded per-layer/per-backend counters at the actual call sites for fused IQ grouped, MMQ GU/Down, native batch/group dequant, oneMath grouped accepted, grouped joint-matrix XMX, and DP4a fallback, with call/group counts, `sum(M)` and maximum M/N/K. This separates path selection without retaining hundreds of thousands of event rows. If service-event mode is used instead, first bound it to aggregated backend/shape groups; do not keep a raw event timeline after extracting evidence.

For a shape sweep, use the actual 4K route histogram as the anchor and compare only row populations that cross its tile boundaries: M buckets around 16/32/64/128/256, then the observed maximum. Keep N/K at the real GU and Down shapes and compare the active path against an explicit non-XMX fallback only if the existing diagnostic can select it safely. For longer prompts, vary the prompt chunk M (1K, 2K, 4K) while preserving identical weights and record the resulting row histogram; a full-prefix 32K aggregate is not an adequate substitute when execution is eight 4K chunks. Report wall time only from the existing speed-eligible quiet gate; do not infer speed from service-event sums or the timing-instrumented diagnostic.

## Prior R313 evidence and reuse limit

The retained R313 report (`research-current-prefill-measured-ledger-next-step-round313-v1.txt`) corrects its earlier labeling: the profile was an actual instrumented B570 32K+16 run, with 129,820 selected events completed and output/health/quit checks. It recorded 5,944 grouped XMX GU and 5,944 grouped XMX Down calls, plus 10,096 native-dequant GU and 10,096 Down calls. Their summed action spans (3.345 s, 1.662 s, 2.545 s, 1.961 s respectively) overlap other work and are not additive wall time, an XMX share of the critical path, a bandwidth figure, or a quiet speed comparison. The instrumentation was not established neutral; the separate quiet native-dequant batching comparison had a qualified 4.66% slower prefill-time result, despite fewer kernels and unchanged copy requests.

R313 is useful evidence that an older instrumented build exercised both grouped XMX and per-expert native dequant at 32K. Reuse stops there: its source/image, route histogram, event population, and call schedule are not the current phase4k image's, it did not capture dense/GDN/QSA work, and its summed spans cannot decide the present critical path. Do not project its counts, event-time proportions, or 32K row shape onto the current sequence of 4K chunks.

No external example is needed for this source-specific path question; no outside performance claim is used.
